title: Honeymoon Destinations: 20 Ideas Sorted by Budget and Season
metaDescription: Honeymoon destination ideas organised by budget tier and time of year — beach, city, adventure and mixed itineraries, with realistic costs.
excerpt: The best honeymoon is rarely the most expensive one. It is the one that matches how the two of you actually like to spend a day.
author: Trypinn Team
content:
Honeymoon planning goes wrong in a predictable way: the destination is chosen from photographs, the budget is set by what feels appropriate rather than what is comfortable, and nobody asks the only question that matters — **how do the two of you actually like to spend a day?**

A couple who get restless lying on a beach should not book an overwater villa for ten nights. A couple who want to do nothing should not book a four-city itinerary. Start there, then use this list.

## First: The Three Questions

**Beach, city, mountains or a mix?** Most honeymoons work best as a **mix** — a few days of activity followed by a few days of nothing, in that order. Ending on a beach means going home rested.

**How much travelling can you face?** You will likely be exhausted after the wedding. A 20-hour journey with two connections starting the day after is a poor idea. Either allow a buffer day or pick somewhere closer.

**What is the real budget?** Including flights, and including the fact that honeymoon spending runs higher than normal travel — you will eat out more, upgrade more, and say yes more. Add 25% to whatever you first estimate.

## Under $3,000 for Two Weeks

**Sri Lanka** — the best value honeymoon in the world for a mixed trip. Tea country by train, safari at Yala, ancient sites at Sigiriya and beaches at Mirissa or Tangalle, all in a small country. Good hotels cost a fraction of their Maldivian equivalents.

**Vietnam** — Hanoi, a bay overnight, then Hoi An and the central coast. Excellent food, very low costs, and beautiful boutique properties.

**Bali and Lombok** — Ubud's rice terraces and a villa with a private pool, then a quieter island. The Canggu–Seminyak corridor is busy; the north and east are not.

**Georgia** — Tbilisi, the Caucasus mountains, and wine country. Underrated, dramatic, and almost no one goes there on honeymoon.

**Portugal** — Lisbon, the Douro Valley, and the Algarve or the Alentejo coast. Easy, romantic and affordable outside peak summer.

**Northern Thailand and the Gulf islands** — Chiang Mai, then Koh Samui or Koh Tao.

![Romantic travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1573790387438-4da905039392?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## $3,000 to $7,000

**Japan** — spring blossom or autumn colour, a ryokan with a private onsen, and Tokyo. Not the obvious honeymoon choice and consistently one of the best.

**Italy** — the Amalfi Coast or Puglia, plus Rome or Florence. Book shoulder season; August is difficult.

**Greece** — Athens plus two islands. Milos and Naxos over Santorini, unless the caldera is specifically the point.

**Morocco** — Marrakesh riads, the Atlas Mountains, a Sahara camp, and Essaouira on the coast. Enormous variety in a short trip.

**Costa Rica** — cloud forest, volcanoes and two coasts. The best option for an active couple.

**Croatia and Montenegro** — Dubrovnik, the islands, and the Bay of Kotor. Sail if the budget allows.

**South Africa** — Cape Town, the Winelands and a safari. Extraordinary value at the top end, and the classic mixed honeymoon.

**Peru** — Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu, then the Amazon or Lake Titicaca. Book Machu Picchu permits early.

## $7,000 and Above

**The Maldives** — the archetype. Overwater villas, extraordinary water, and genuinely nothing to do. Best combined with a few days in Sri Lanka first if you want variety. Ten nights of nothing suits fewer couples than the photographs suggest.

**French Polynesia** — Bora Bora, Moorea and Tahiti. More dramatic landscapes than the Maldives, further from everywhere, and more expensive.

**Kenya or Tanzania** — safari plus Zanzibar. The best combination of adventure and beach available anywhere. Time it around the migration if wildlife is the priority.

**The Seychelles** — granite boulders, extraordinary beaches, and more to do than the Maldives.

**Switzerland and the Dolomites** — an alpine honeymoon. Mountain hotels, rail journeys and hiking. Perfect for couples who do not want a beach.

**New Zealand** — a self-drive across both islands. The best honeymoon for couples who want to be outdoors every day.

**Iceland and Greenland** — northern lights in winter, midnight sun in summer. Dramatic rather than relaxing.

![Romantic travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578922746465-3a80a228f223?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## By Season

**December to March** — the Maldives, Sri Lanka's south, Thailand's Andaman coast, Vietnam's south, New Zealand, South Africa, Argentina, Kenya, Zanzibar

**April to June** — Japan, Italy, Greece, Portugal, Croatia, Bali, Morocco, Peru, Iceland

**July and August** — Iceland, Norway, Canada, New Zealand's winter, Indonesia, the Gulf islands of Thailand, East Africa for the migration, Scotland

**September to November** — Italy and Greece at their best, Japan's autumn, Croatia, Morocco, Vietnam's north, South Africa, the Seychelles

## The Practical Details People Forget

**Name on the ticket.** If one partner is changing their name, book flights in the name on the passport that will be used to travel. Changing a name on a passport before the honeymoon is a race most people lose.

**Travel insurance.** Buy it when you book, not before you fly, so cancellation cover applies for the whole run-up.

**Tell the hotels.** Say it is a honeymoon at the time of booking and again on arrival. Upgrades, room amenities and small gestures are common and cost nothing to ask for.

**Build a buffer day.** Do not fly the morning after the wedding. One day of recovery makes an enormous difference to how the first half of the trip feels.

**Do not over-schedule.** The most common honeymoon regret is a packed itinerary that left no time to simply be together. Two activities a day, maximum.

**Split the planning.** Honeymoons are frequently planned by one person while the other plans the wedding, which produces a trip that suits one of you. Even a single shared session choosing the shape of it — and a shared plan you can both see and add to — changes the result. **Trypinn** is straightforward for this: build the days together, keep the bookings in one place, and neither of you is the only one holding the itinerary.

## The One Piece of Advice Worth Keeping

Spend the money on **fewer, better days** rather than more days. Ten nights somewhere you love, in a place you would not normally book, beats sixteen nights of compromise — and beats a punishing itinerary that has you packing every other morning.

You will not remember how many places you went. You will remember one specific evening, and you should plan for that.
